$comment: Initial consent — the first corporate act. Note consent_issue is split into two mutually exclusive variants so the reference to the vesting agreement only exists when that document does. A single clause with an unconditional cross-reference was the original defect this split fixes.

clauses.title: Adoption of Governing Documents
clauses.rationale: The governing document has no force until adopted. Founders routinely sign an operating agreement and never record the adoption.
clauses.body: The {{ownerTerm}} adopt the {{govDoc}} attached hereto, effective {{date}}, and ratify the filing of the {{charterDoc}} with the Secretary of State of {{formStateLong}} and all acts taken by the organizer or incorporator in connection with that filing.

clauses.title: Election of Initial Directors
clauses.rationale: The incorporator's authority ends when the board is seated. Until then no one has authority to act for the corporation.
clauses.body: The following persons are elected to serve as the initial directors of the Company until their successors are elected and qualified: {{founderList}}. The incorporator’s authority terminates upon this election as provided in <<xr:charter_incorporator>>.

clauses.title: Issuance of Interests
clauses.rationale: Variant used when the package includes a vesting agreement, so the reference to the vesting terms always resolves.
clauses.body: The Company shall issue the interests set forth on Schedule A to the {{ownerTerm}} in exchange for the contributions described in <<xr:gov_units>>, subject to the vesting terms of <<xr:vest_schedule>> and the repurchase right in <<xr:vest_repurchase>>.

clauses.title: Issuance of Interests
clauses.rationale: Variant used when no vesting agreement is generated. Identical to the vesting variant except that it makes no reference to a document that does not exist.
clauses.body: The Company shall issue the interests set forth on Schedule A to the {{ownerTerm}} in exchange for the contributions described in <<xr:gov_units>>.

clauses.title: Ratification of IP Assignment
clauses.rationale: Recording the assignment in the minute book is what makes it findable in diligence three years later.
clauses.body: The Company accepts the assignment of intellectual property made under <<xr:ipa_assign>> and directs that a copy of the executed assignment, together with each founder’s Exhibit A, be maintained in the Company’s records.

clauses.title: Appointment of Officers
clauses.rationale: Counterparties and banks ask who is authorized to sign. This is the document they are asking for.
clauses.body: {{founder1}} is appointed as the Company’s initial {{principalTitle}}, authorized to execute agreements, open accounts, and make filings on the Company’s behalf, subject to any limitation in <<xr:@approval>>.

clauses.title: Banking Resolution
clauses.rationale: Banks require a resolution before opening an account, and a separate account is the first thing a court looks at in a veil-piercing analysis.
clauses.body: The Company is authorized to open one or more deposit accounts in its name, and {{founder1}} is authorized to execute the account documentation. Company funds shall not be commingled with the personal funds of any {{ownerSing}}.

clauses.title: Tax Identification
clauses.rationale: The EIN gates the bank account and payroll, so it is on the critical path for almost everything else.
clauses.body: The Company is authorized to apply for an Employer Identification Number on IRS Form SS-4 and to register for the state tax accounts required in {{opStateLong}}, as calendared in <<xr:cal_ein>>.

clauses.title: Fiscal Year and Accounting Method
clauses.rationale: Set once at formation. Changing the fiscal year later generally requires IRS consent.
clauses.body: The Company adopts a fiscal year ending December 31 and the cash method of accounting, in each case subject to change by approval under <<xr:@approval>> and to any requirement of the Internal Revenue Code.

clauses.title: Acknowledgment of 83(b) Deadline
clauses.rationale: The Company cannot file the election for the founder, but it can document that the founder was told about the deadline.
clauses.body: Each founder acknowledges that any Section 83(b) election with respect to interests issued under this consent must be filed by that founder within thirty (30) days of {{date}}, as described in <<xr:b83_instructions>>, and that the Company cannot make the filing on their behalf.

clauses.title: Authorization to Qualify in Other States
clauses.rationale: Gives the officer express authority to make the foreign qualification filing rather than doing it on assumed authority.
clauses.body: The {{principalTitle}} is authorized to qualify the Company to transact business in {{opStateLong}} and in any other state where its activities require registration, and to appoint a registered agent in each such state, as described in <<xr:fq_statement>>.
